title: Best Women's Golf Shoes UK
short: Nine women's golf shoes worn over full rounds in different conditions, spiked and spikeless, compared on comfort, grip, stability and waterproofing.
intro: Your feet are the basis of your swing, and a golf shoe only shows its worth over hours of walking on real turf. This guide compares women's shoes tested by Golf Monthly, whose women's editor Alison Root heads up all women's product testing with gear testers Katie Dawkins and Carly Cummins. Every shoe here was personally worn by a member of the team over a number of rounds and in different conditions, to judge comfort, grip, stability, waterproofing, sizing and how it looks on the course. All nine picks are covered, eight spikeless and one spiked.

products.name: Street Vibe (women's)
products.best_for: Golfers who want a sneaker-style spikeless shoe that performs in any conditions
products.key_spec: Spikeless, ECCO-TEX waterproof membrane, E-DTS NET outsole, removable insole, US sizes 4-11.5
products.summary: Golf Monthly's top pick for 2026, described as a near flawless spikeless shoe that blends a modern, high-end sneaker look with premium on-course performance. The E-DTS NET outsole gives impressive multi-directional traction and a secure grip through the swing, and there is an out-of-the-box broken-in feel from an ultra-soft tongue and plush heel padding, plus a removable insole for adjustable width. The tester found it very difficult to fault, with limited colour choice the only drawback listed.
pros: Hybrid flexibility, works on and off the course
products.search: Ecco Street Vibe women's golf shoe

products.name: Slip-ins Blade Tour (women's)
products.best_for: Golfers who want hands-free entry, cushioning and spiked grip in wet conditions
products.key_spec: Spiked, replaceable Softspikes Tour Flex Pro, Slip-ins heel with Heel Pillow, Arch Fit insole, waterproof, US sizes 5.5-11
products.summary: A no-nonsense spiked shoe that Golf Monthly found super convenient and very comfortable. The Slip-ins technology genuinely allows hands-free entry while a Heel Pillow holds the foot in place, and the replaceable Softspikes outsole gave exceptional grip, keeping the tester locked in even when swinging aggressively on damp, uneven lies. The synthetic Clarino upper is fully waterproof with a one-year warranty. The fit ran slightly roomy around the toes for the tester, so half sizes are worth considering, and the styling is subdued.
products.search: Skechers Slip-ins Blade Tour women's golf shoe

products.name: Pro/SL Women's (2026)
products.best_for: Golfers who walk most of their rounds and want light, waterproof spikeless grip
products.key_spec: Spikeless, Z-TEC upper, ARCTrax/SL sole, StratoFOAM heel, OrthoLite FitBed, waterproof, sizes 3-9
products.summary: FootJoy's staple spikeless shoe, refreshed for its tenth year with a sportier look and 29% less weight. Golf Monthly calls it one of, if not the most comfortable shoes you can buy, with a 3D moulded collar, cushioned heel, a roomier toe box and a FitBed that moulds to the foot. The multi-layered upper anchors the foot through the swing and the spikeless sole holds on wet grass and rough. The athletic styling is less versatile than shoes designed to be worn anywhere.
cons: Style is not as versatile as shoes that can be worn anywhere
products.search: FootJoy Pro SL women's golf shoe 2026

products.name: Quantum Women's
products.best_for: Regular walkers who put cushioning first over 18 holes
products.key_spec: Spikeless, SofFOAM midsole, premium leather, reinforced heel, one-year waterproof guarantee, sizes 3-9
products.summary: Golf Monthly's most comfortable women's golf shoe, largely thanks to a SofFOAM midsole described as the softest cushioning FootJoy has made, combined with plush leather and a reinforced heel for support. Comfort is evident from the moment they are unboxed, and they are easy to clean. The look is athletic and simple, the grip is good, and golfers worried about the spikeless design are pointed to the Pro/SL as an alternative.
cons: Not as versatile as other golf shoes for wearing on and off the course

products.name: Fresh Foam Contend v3 (women's)
products.best_for: Golfers who want out-of-the-box comfort and year-round waterproofing at an accessible price
products.key_spec: Spikeless, Fresh Foam cushioning, waterproof upper, lightweight, sizes 4-9
products.summary: Golf Monthly's best-value pick, comfortable from the moment it comes out of the box with no break-in period. The Fresh Foam cushioning is tuned slightly firmer than New Balance's running shoes to stabilise the swing, and a locked-in heel and high-traction spikeless outsole gave grip that rivals spiked models on wet or uneven lies. Built-in arch support is minimal, so golfers needing more structure may want to add an insole.
pros: Excellent stability for a spikeless shoe, very secure throughout the swing
Comfortable straight out of the box
Waterproof and lightweight, a great choice for golf all year round
cons: Golfers needing extra arch support may need to add an insole
products.search: New Balance Fresh Foam Contend v3 women's golf shoe

products.name: Women's Halo Hybrid 'Golf Trip'
products.best_for: Golfers who walk and want one shoe for the course, travel and everyday wear
products.key_spec: Spikeless, oversized soft sole, fully waterproof, lightweight, sizes 2.5-8.5
products.summary: Given a five-star review by Golf Monthly's tester, who found it lightweight, very comfortable and superb-looking. It is built for golfers who walk, with a casual look that works from the range to the clubhouse or a dog walk, yet the spikeless outsole gives reliable multi-directional traction and stability through the swing with plenty of cushioning. The sizing comes up a touch tight, and it comes in one colour.
pros: Supersized soft sole gives incredible traction
cons: Sizing comes up a touch tight
products.search: Under Armour Halo Hybrid Golf Trip women's golf shoe

products.name: G.112 Stripe Kiltie (women's)
products.best_for: Golfers who want a head-turning shoe that also works in the clubhouse and beyond
products.key_spec: Spikeless, water-repellent PU leather upper, optional kiltie, EVA midsole, machine-washable massaging insole, sizes 3-9
products.summary: Golf Monthly calls this arguably the highlight of G/FORE's women's range, with clean lines, stripe accents and an optional fold-over kiltie. Comfort is top-tier straight out of the box thanks to a snug heel lock, breathable mesh lining and a cushioned midsole, plus G/FORE's machine-washable insole that massages the foot as you walk. The low-drop design and updated spikeless tread gave exceptional stability, though the fabric collar needs wiping down to stay pristine.
cons: Might not be the easiest to keep clean
products.search: G/FORE G.112 Stripe Kiltie women's golf shoe

products.name: 327 Women's Golf Shoe
products.best_for: Golfers who want a lifestyle-sneaker look that goes straight from course to everyday wear
products.key_spec: Spikeless, waterproof microfibre leather upper, NDurance rubber outsole, Cush+ insole, EVA midsole, sizes 3.5-8.5
products.summary: Golf Monthly found no shoe blends modern sneaker style and golf quite like the 327. A waterproof microfibre leather upper with suede-like accents sits over a moulded Cush+ insole, EVA midsole and plush heel collar that gave blister-free comfort over 18 holes, while the NDurance spikeless outsole wraps up the toe and heel and locks the stance in place. They run small, so the tester advises going up half a size, and the look will not suit those who prefer traditional styling.
cons: Not for those who prefer traditional styling

products.name: Avant 2 Ladies
products.best_for: Golfers who want a classic leather look at a budget-friendly price
products.key_spec: Full-grain leather upper, PROFOAM midsole, carbon rubber outsole, one-year waterproof warranty, sizes 3-8
products.summary: Named among the best budget golf shoes by Golf Monthly, with the vintage look of classic leather footwear and a one-year waterproof warranty. The PROFOAM midsole gives plush, spongy cushioning straight out of the box, the build is light, and the carbon rubber outsole gives solid traction in wet or dry conditions. The toe box is slightly narrow, so it may not suit wider feet.
pros: Sturdy sole designed to work in wet or dry course conditions
Refined aesthetics over the last iteration
cons: Narrow toe shape may not suit women with wider feet

guide.a: Golf Monthly says spiked shoes are likely to give more lateral stability in soft, wet conditions or on a hilly course, while spikeless shoes are lighter, more breathable and best suited to firm, dry ground, and can be worn indoors in the clubhouse. Advances in traction mean the best spikeless shoes now perform well all year, which is why the spikeless Ecco Street Vibe is the top pick. The Skechers Slip-ins Blade Tour is the spiked option here.

Golf Monthly calls it essential if you play in a colder, wetter climate, since there is nothing worse than soaking wet feet mid-round. Most shoes here are waterproof, with FootJoy's Quantum and Puma's Avant 2 carrying a one-year waterproof guarantee, while the G/FORE G.112's upper is described as water repellent. Also think about cleaning: breathable fabrics can be harder to wipe down than leather or synthetic uppers.

guide.q: How should women's golf shoes fit?
guide.a: Too tight and you get blisters on the heel and big toe, too loose and you lose connection with the ground. Golf Monthly advises trying shoes on with the socks you will wear and doing a walking test. Its testers also flag sizing quirks: the New Balance 327 runs small (go up half a size), the Under Armour Halo Hybrid comes up a touch tight, the Skechers Blade Tour is roomy around the toes, and the Puma Avant 2 has a narrow toe box.

guide.q: Which women's golf shoes can be worn off the course?
guide.a: Several are designed for it. The Under Armour Halo Hybrid is described as a go-anywhere shoe, the New Balance 327 passes as a lifestyle sneaker, the Ecco Street Vibe has a relaxed streetwear look and the G/FORE G.112 would not look out of place in a restaurant. The FootJoy Pro/SL and Quantum are rated less versatile away from the course.
